prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 2D merge · Clinic schedule (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Time" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Monday" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Tuesday" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Cardiology clinic (Dr. I" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Dermatology" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Staff training — closed " spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Time" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 49px
  col 2: header "Monday › Room A" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 419px
  col 3: header "Monday › Room B" · longest unbreakable word 97px · one-line width 97px
  col 4: header "Tuesday › Room A" · longest unbreakable word 109px · one-line width 109px
  col 5: header "Tuesday › Room B" · longest unbreakable word 99px · one-line width 406px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 682px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 681px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Show the clinic schedule by time, day and room, including shared closures and activities that span time slots.","reading":"Readers scan down the time column, then across the Monday and Tuesday room columns to locate or compare activities. Merged cells show when an activity covers multiple times or rooms.","groups":["Monday Room A and Room B belong under the Monday header; Tuesday Room A and Room B belong under Tuesday.","All four room columns play the same scheduling role and should remain easy to compare.","The time column identifies each row and can be narrower than the activity columns."],"keep_intact":["Time labels such as 09:00 and 10:00","Room identifiers and day names","Names, abbreviations and individual words where the available width permits"],"may_wrap":["Long clinic descriptions at word boundaries","The staff training closure across its merged cell","Activities spanning two time slots can use the combined row height for wrapped text"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [70, 153, 153, 153, 152] · table 682×316px · row heights [39, 39, 59, 59, 118] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [69, 184, 124, 129, 173] · table 680×303px · row heights [39, 39, 66, 39, 118] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [69, 134, 124, 159, 193] · table 680×316px · row heights [39, 39, 91, 54, 92] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Constraint adjustments applied: r0B: scaled down from 684px to fit 681px
r0C: scaled down from 684px to fit 681px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
